# md2edrawmind

> Turn AI-generated Markdown notes containing LaTeX formulas into Word (.docx) files that
> mind-mapping apps — verified against EdrawMind 12.2.2 — import with every formula still
> readable and the heading hierarchy intact. Runs 100% offline.

Repository: https://github.com/socoolgzh-max/md2edrawmind
License: MIT
Language: Python (converter, GUI, CLI) + JavaScript (MathJax formula rendering)
Platform: Windows (verified); path detection is Windows-oriented

## Problem it solves

Mind-mapping apps parse Markdown as plain text, so `$...$` LaTeX is mangled on import:

- Markdown import: formulas stay literal text
- HTML import that uses a cloud "smart parse": formulas become tags, simplified Chinese is
  converted to traditional, hierarchy collapses
- Word native equations (OMML): the Word importer flattens them into characters, e.g.
  `\lim_{n \to \infty} S_n = S` becomes `limn→∞Sn=S`
- SVG formulas: rejected by the importer
- Working route: render each formula to PNG, embed the pictures in a .docx, and import that
  .docx locally. Requires `w:outlineLvl` in the document XML for hierarchy to survive.

Additional app quirk: a formula placed in the middle of a topic's text is filed as a
"comment". Hence the default layout mode `tail` moves formulas to the end of each topic.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/socoolgzh-max/md2edrawmind && cd md2edrawmind
pip install -r requirements.txt
npm install
python -m md2edrawmind check
```

Requirements: Python 3.9+, Node.js 18+, Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.

## Use

```
python -m md2edrawmind serve                  # local GUI on http://127.0.0.1:8787
python -m md2edrawmind convert notes.md       # writes notes.docx
python -m md2edrawmind convert notes.md --limit 46 --outline
```

Then, in the mind-mapping app: Import -> Word -> select the .docx.

CLI layout modes: `--mix tail` (default), `--mix own`, `--mix keep`.

## Key files

- md2edrawmind/parser.py — Markdown/LaTeX parsing, topic tree, formula placement strategies
- md2edrawmind/docx_writer.py — w:outlineLvl hierarchy, inline formula pictures, splitting
- md2edrawmind/pipeline.py — orchestrates parse -> render -> slice -> docx
- md2edrawmind/server.py — local stdlib HTTP server for the GUI (upload, SSE progress, download)
- md2edrawmind/cli.py — convert / serve / check / install-tools
- tools/render.js — MathJax -> SVG, formula sheet layout, PNG slicing
- tools/mathjax.js — MathJax v3 wrapper
- tests/test_parser.py, tests/smoke_gui.py — unit tests and GUI end-to-end smoke test
- docs/FINDINGS.md — reverse-engineering notes about the target app's import behaviour

## Known limits

- Formulas are images inside the map: they display but cannot be edited as equations,
  because the app's Word importer does not support OMML.
- PDF export from the app still carries its trial watermark (PNG/JPG do not).
- Multi-line math environments (`aligned`, `cases`) render as a single line.
- EdrawMind free tier caps Word/HTML/Markdown imports at 50 topics; use `--limit` to split.
